sourceClaims.fact: InitializeOnLoad static constructor attempts autoStart, then registers play/quitting/reload callbacks. before/afterAssemblyReload bodies are empty comments. They do not explicitly stop listener, close it, remove descriptor or shutdown dispatcher. Actual old-domain/native socket lifetime is not established by these comments.

Start picks port, initializes own main-thread dispatcher, warms token, marksrunningtrue and openslistener; only then descriptor, watchdog, ServerStarted. Startup restores auto-tick only AFTER Start returns. An initial bind failure prevents watchdog arming and auto-tick restoration in that attempt.

Start catch setsrunningfalse, calls listener.Stop and nulls it; no explicit listener.Close or dispatcher.Shutdown there. Stop returns immediately when notrunning, otherwise does Close/deleteDescriptor/Shutdown. Thus later owner Stop/Restart is not source proof that an already failed-start dispatcher was removed. This is a cleanup risk, not proof of the actual socket holder.

Watchdog subscribes EditorApplication.update only when armed. It skips compiling/updating and closes an existing dead listener before reopen. It cannot be assumed to recover an initial Start failure before ArmWatchdog, nor to run when update callbacks are blocked.

Port0 scans first available Editor range using a disposable HttpListener with the SAME wildcard prefix; explicit port skips scan. Probe is released before actual OpenListener, with no atomic reservation or scan retry after actualbind failure. Underlying race/reservation/release delay possible but not observed. No TcpListener/IPv4-only-probe claim. Actual config port mode pending.

StartedAt/LastHeartbeat initialize at descriptor creation, not OS process birth. Same PID can have new server descriptor after reload. Startup removes stale descriptor only if PID gone/lookup throws; livePID stale file is not automatically cleared. Descriptor creation is after listeneropen in normal Start sequence, but an existing/rewritten file alone cannot correlate which bind attempt currently serves HTTP.

Heartbeat refresh is called by /api/status and detailed status handling; no periodic heartbeat update registered in inspected Editor server/startup. Watchdog/update ticks are different. A descriptor stale since creation alone is not proof deadserver/mainthreadblock. Query failure, no requests or descriptorwrite failure can leave stale data; write failures log warning.

Dispatcher registers ProcessWorkQueue on EditorApplication.update and unregisters on Shutdown. Detailed editor_status is main-thread required and shares exec gate. It can wait behind running work or an unpumped main thread even if basic HTTP status is reachable; timeouts do not prove callback identity/cause.

GET/api/status is an existing authenticated loopback metadata endpoint directly calling GetServerStatus without exec gate or mainthread dispatch. It updates descriptor heartbeat and returns ready/settling/dialog state snapshot. A successful reply distinguishes a responding listener from command-dispatch failure, not fully working compiler/game. If listenerbind failed it cannot resurrect it.

Existing Window/Pipeline Start Server / Stop Server menu and existing manager inspector Start/Stop/Restart are supported UI lifecycle surfaces. Startup and manager classes are internal despite public members, so they are not public C# APIs callable from ordinary project code. Stop menu disabled when IsRunning false; inspector Restart can attempt Stop+Start, with failed-start cleanup caveat. Settings menu creates asset if absent; do not open it as a no-change probe.

set_autotick is mainthread-required and needs a working transport; it cannot bootstrap a failed listener. Runtime-pipeline settings commands configure Player driver, not Editor listener. No dedicated Editor server restart/port command found in inspected shipped attributes; a CLI menu/eval request also cannot repair its own unreachable HTTP transport.

Docs describe localhost/IPv4 loopback prefix binds, while actual source binds wildcard prefix and enforces loopback/auth in request handling. Use pinned source for actual binding behavior; do not turn doc examples into cause evidence.
